note: What this file is: the third critique of the notice corner (log 32): three critics (composition and light, before the repaint, period and story) and a skeptic, as they wrote it. Session folders are shortened to SCRATCH, KIT and REPO.

critics.summary:
Verdict: the composition holds and the notice clearly wins. Most of the listed fixes work. Two did not take effect, and one fix from the last round changed nothing. Nothing I found is a must-fix, but four should-fix items are worth one more preview before the paid repaint.

What the eye does, judged at phone size and from a blurred copy: 1st, the notice. It is the one big bright shape, holding 65% of the brightest 3% of the frame, and it is 3.2 times as bright as the frame's average. 2nd, the drum: a big orange cylinder covering 3.9% of the frame, almost twice the notice's 2.1%. 3rd, the gas lamp's amber head at the top of the notice column. 4th, the lantern on the chair seat.

The story props read as one touching group. Both columns line up:
- notice column: lamp 0.81, notice 0.80, lantern 0.76 and pail 0.77 across;
- pit column: wheels 0.61, gates 0.60 and drum 0.57 across.
The top third holds the lamp head and the winding wheels. The chair stands under the notice (0.75 across against 0.80), its seat shows and the lantern is lit.

Fixes that hold:
- The orange oval on the wall is gone (0.24 to 0.15 brightness).
- The black lamp foot is gone: the lowest visible lamp-post pixel is at 0.466 down, behind the board.
- The chair is now 0.2 darker than the paper along their shared edge.
- The lantern glass is amber (0.52), with a dark frame and no clipping.
- The drum mouth fell from 0.76 to 0.32, with no orange band showing outside the drum.
- The handcart overlaps the bins by 37 px.

Did not take effect:
- No new lit window on the left: nothing in the left houses got brighter by even 0.01.
- The corner lamp glass is amber but still one flat tone (0.51 ± 0.03 in every row). The mantle never shows through.
- The colliery yard light made no difference: the doorway behind the shut gates is still 0.028 (0.027 before), so the gates are lost.

Worse than the still before:
- The whole frame got darker: average 0.248 down to 0.212, against 0.323 in the picture the user liked. The ground is a dim brown floor.
- The chair is now so dark that its legs are darker than the pavement (0.16 against 0.20). In a squint it drops out, where the user's picture has a white chair as the second-brightest shape.

New faults:
- The drum mouth is a flat, saturated orange disc with a pale ring as bright as the notice paper.
- The new left lamp's head is squeezed between two downpipes, 11 and 12 px away.

Balance: the left half is still light, but closer to the reference. By my measures, the left half holds:
- 33% of the above-average light (reference 39%, previous still 22%);
- 35% of the local contrast (reference 41%).
Most of that gain came from the right side getting darker. The cheapest real fix is the fire's warm patch on the road. It is in the right place (0.37, 0.70) but only 0.29 bright, against 0.63 in the reference.

findings.title: The whole frame is a third darker than the liked picture, and the ground is dim brown
findings.where: Whole frame, worst in the bottom third: pavement 0.45-1.0 across, 0.88-1.0 down; near-left road 0-0.33 across, 0.83-1.0 down; left houses 0-0.45 across, 0.2-0.5 down
findings.what: Frame average 0.212 (previous still 0.248, the liked picture 0.323). Bottom third, left/right: 0.19/0.22 (previous still 0.25/0.32, reference 0.35/0.33). Pavement 0.24, colour 75,59,43 (reference 0.35, 92,88,89). Near-left road 0.19, colour 62,47,35 (reference 0.27, 68,67,74). Left houses 0.19 (reference 0.26). Sky top-left 0.28 (reference 0.40). Below mid-frame only 15% of pixels are bluer than red (reference 43%). The notice is unchanged against the reference (0.68 against 0.69), so the notice's lead over everything else (3.2 times the frame average, against about 2.1 in the reference) comes from a darker world.
findings.why: The painter copies light and dark, so the painting will be a darker, more night-like picture than the one the user liked. On a phone, the quiet side's brick and cobbles at 0.19 sink into mud. The film page also adds a 0.3 vignette, which darkens the edges further, including the quiet left side. A dark, brown ground also blunts rule 6's contrast of warm people's lights against a cool night.
findings.fix: Raise only the cool sky light, not any warm light. An earlier critic named dusk_world's Background strength (1.4 to about 2.0); I have not checked that node. Try it in a --preview. Targets: frame average 0.26-0.30; notice still at least 2.5 times the average; top third under 0.36 (the checker's limit); bottom third about 0.27; red-minus-blue on the bottom third away from the drum at +0.06 or less. This also adds weight to the left half, which is mostly lit by the sky.

findings.title: The drum's mouth is now a flat, saturated orange disc with a pale salmon ring as bright as the notice
findings.where: Drum top, 0.46-0.67 across, 0.626-0.648 down (the drum prop)
findings.what: Mouth: 0.32 brightness (down from 0.76, meeting the 0.45 target), but colour 137,71,13 with saturation 0.94 and one even tone and a sharp edge. It looks like orange paint or liquid filling a tub, not soot with a glow deep inside. No coals show. The lip ring is still 0.74, colour 244,177,147, against a target of 0.65 or less. The notice paper's median is 0.736, so the ring is as bright as the subject. It forms the 4th-largest patch of the brightest 3%, an ellipse outline right beside the notice's lower-left corner. The drum's lit inside is now the only thing the liner fix changed; the liner does sit inside the wall, with no band showing outside.
findings.why: The painter is told not to paint flames, so it will copy an orange lid or a bowl of liquid, and the film's live flames will stand on it. A pale ring at the notice's brightness, inside the story group, competes with the notice's edge.
findings.fix: (1) Keep the drum object: line 124, drum = place_prop('brazier-drum.glb', ...). After line 128 add light_reaches(bpy.data.objects['brazier_light'], drum.children_recursive, only=False), the same skip used for the lantern at line 186. The fire's light then stops lighting the drum's own rim from 0.4 m above; the film's live flames light it instead. (2) Make the liner dark at the top and glowing only low down. Lower its glow from 0.15 to about 0.05 on a near-black base, or drive its emission strength with a top-to-bottom gradient (strong at the coals, zero 5 cm below the rim). Targets: mouth average 0.15-0.25, visibly darker just under the rim than deeper in; lip 0.55 or less; saturation under 0.7.

findings.title: The shut colliery gates are still lost in a pure-black doorway; the yard light changed nothing
findings.where: 0.57-0.64 across, 0.41-0.47 down, beside where the street's lines meet (0.684, 0.439)
findings.what: Doorway 0.028 in this still against 0.027 in the previous one: colliery_yard_light (lines 255-258, 40 W at Blender (0, 77, 8.3)) made no measurable difference. Gates (prop mask) 0.050, with the 90th percentile at 0.085. The reference's doorway is 0.131, colour 30,34,41, with the gate bars clearly in silhouette. At phone size and in a squint the gates do not show; only faint railings show against the brick at either side.
findings.why: The brief names the shut gates as part of the picture: they are the lockout in one image, and the middle of the 'pit' column (wheels, gates, drum; rule 7). The street's lines lead the eye straight to this spot, so a black hole there is a strong dark accent. The painter will fill it with something it invents, such as an open tunnel or a lit door, or leave it flat black.
findings.fix: First find what fills the doorway in street.blend (a dark material or the building's inside). I could not open it. Then do one of these: give the doorway's back face a dim cool emission of about 0.1, or move the yard light to just inside the opening (about y 73.5, 2 m behind the gate line), raise it to about 300 W, colour (0.7, 0.8, 1.0), shadows off. Target: doorway 0.08-0.13, still below the frame average, with the gate bars visible against it. Painter words as backup: 'the colliery gates are shut; a dim yard shows through the bars, no open tunnel, no lit door'.

findings.title: The left half is still light. The cheapest cure is the fire's road patch; the promised extra lit window is missing
findings.where: Left half: the road patch at about 0.37 across, 0.70 down; the left houses 0.05-0.42 across, 0.25-0.48 down; the left lamps at 0.36 and 0.42 across, 0.38-0.50 down
findings.what:
The checker gives 36% (aim 40-48%). My left-half shares, this still / previous still / reference:
- brightness: 48.6 / 45.2 / 49.0%
- above-average light: 33.4 / 21.8 / 39.4%
- local contrast: 34.8 / 31.0 / 40.6%
- edges: 38.3 / 36.5 / 45.2%
The right half's average fell from 0.273 to 0.218 while the left's barely moved (0.224 to 0.206), so most of the gain came from the right getting darker.
The fire's road patch is in the reference's place: its peak is 0.29 at (0.37, 0.70), against the reference's 0.63 at (0.35, 0.71). It is only 1.43 times the road around it (reference 1.77) and 1.4 times the frame average (reference 1.95).
No window on the left got brighter between the two stills (no spot brighter by even 0.01). The previous still's log lit only one window. light_left_windows keeps every second candidate ([::2]), so with two or fewer candidates it lights only one; this is my guess, because this still's log line has not been written yet.
The reference's left lamp is nearer (0.23 across), bright (0.59) and throws a glow on the wall. Ours are both small and far (0.36 and 0.42 across) and add no glow on the wall: the area round the new lamp's head measures 0.168 in both stills.
findings.why: Rule 10: the quiet side should be quiet, not empty. The reference's warm cobbles also lead the eye from the bottom-left entry to the drum and the notice. A painter usually flattens fine far detail, so small dim things on the left will weigh even less once painted.
findings.fix: (a) Line 67, ROAD_GLOW_WATTS 250 to about 500-700. Target: patch peak 0.40-0.45 at about (0.37, 0.70); the checker's warm share still 3% or less (now 2.5%). (b) In light_left_windows, drop the [::2] or widen its box so 2-3 windows actually light, at emission 1.2, spread between 0.05 and 0.42 across. Check the log's 'lit windows:' line. (c) Give the new left lamp a visible bright core and a little glow on the wall (see the lamp-glass finding). Raise left_lamp_light from 10 W to about 40-60 W so it lights the brick round it. Re-run the checker after each step; stop at about 42%.

findings.title: The chair is now too dark to read as the empty white chair
findings.where: Chair, 0.61-0.89 across, 0.61-0.88 down: seat 0.66-0.85 across, 0.725-0.765 down; legs 0.60-0.90 across, 0.77-0.88 down
findings.what: The tint went to 0.18; the critics proposed 0.34 or 0.42. Chair average 0.32 (previous still 0.54). Seat top 0.36, colour 102,88,77. The legs average 0.16, darker than the pavement right around them (0.20). Chair back where it crosses the notice: 0.51 against 0.71 for the paper beside it, a good separation, and the brightest 5% of the chair (0.66) stays under the paper's median (0.74). The front edge of the seat is still the 3rd-largest bright patch (0.17% of the frame, 0.54), so the seat does show. But in a blurred phone-size view the chair almost vanishes into the ground. In the reference the white chair's seat measures 0.74 and is the second-brightest shape, carrying the notice column down from notice to lantern to chair to pail.
findings.why: Rule 9: the empty chair made for a person is how the shot shows the missing person. It now reads as a grey-blue chair the colour of the pavement. The painter will copy a mid-grey chair, not a worn white one.
findings.fix: Line 160: tint (0.18, 0.18, 0.18) to about (0.26, 0.26, 0.25). In the same --preview, check the chair back against the paper beside it. If the gap falls under 0.12, also make brazier_light skip the chair (add chair.children_recursive to the light_reaches(..., only=False) call from the drum fix). The back is lit mainly by that light from 0.6 m, while the seat is lit by the lantern. Targets: seat top at least 0.45; legs at least as light as the pavement round them (0.20 or more); chair back at least 0.12 below the paper beside it; the chair's brightest 5% at 0.70 or less.

findings.title: The notice's top is too warm, and the film's fire light sits three quarters of the way up the notice
findings.where: Notice paper, 0.71-0.88 across, 0.51-0.65 down
findings.what:
Paper only (letters left out), in six bands from top to bottom, brightness / red-minus-blue:
- this still: 0.754/+0.259, 0.764/+0.255, 0.749/+0.266, 0.763/+0.271, 0.811/+0.262, 0.777/+0.296
- reference: 0.626/+0.101 rising to 0.736/+0.315
So the problem is that the top is warm, not that the bottom is cool. Across, the paper dims from 0.80 at its left to 0.71 at its right.
In notice-corner.js, fireLight (line 87) sits at Blender z 2.93, 73% of the way up the notice (2.37-3.14), so the film's top will be warm too. By my geometry the film's noticeGlow (cone half-angle 25 degrees, penumbra 0.9, aimed 4 cm under the notice's bottom edge) lights about the lower 40% of the notice and almost nothing at its middle. I did not render the film.
findings.why: Rule 6: cool at the top, warm at the bottom. Its source is the people's own fire. In the film the notice wears its own surface, so only the page's lights decide this; the checker's 0.08 against 0.10 on the still does not reach the film.
findings.fix: In notice-corner.js, put fireLight at the flames' height rather than Blender's: for example coals.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0, 0.25, 0)) (about z 2.63) instead of fromBlender(shot.fire_light). Or cut its intensity from 4 to about 2.5 and let noticeGlow carry the warmth. Then judge the film's end frame. Targets: top band red-minus-blue +0.15 or less; bottom band at least +0.10 warmer than the top; nothing on the paper above 0.85.

findings.title: The corner lamp's glass is amber but still one flat tone, and the street's lamps now come in two colours
findings.where: Corner lamp glass, 0.77-0.85 across, 0.20-0.29 down; left lamps at 0.34-0.38 across (new) and 0.41-0.43 across (the street's own), 0.38-0.43 down
findings.what: Corner glass: average 0.50, saturation 0.62, colour 171,120,64. Every row from 0.24 to 0.28 down measures 0.51 ± 0.03, with no brighter core. The 'part see-through, the mantle shows' change made no visible difference. The new left lamp's glass is the same: 0.50, colour 172,119,63. The street's own lamp just beside it is 0.81, colour 226,202,174, with a visible bright core and 7% clipped. So the nearer lamp is dimmer than the farther one, and the two differ in colour. Reference lamp glass: 0.70, colour 211,175,127, saturation 0.39, a flame visible. The corner lamp head is also smaller since it moved back. It is still the strongest small eye-catch at the top of the notice column.
findings.why: Rule 7's notice column starts with this lamp. A flat amber card reads as a paper shade, and the painter will copy two kinds of street lamp in one street.
findings.fix: In the glass branches (lines 198-200 and 217-219), get the transparency to show: in Blender 5.x EEVEE that may also need the material's render method set to blended or dithered. Or give the glass's glow a top-to-bottom gradient peaking at the mantle height (3.27 m). Use a paler amber, about make_glow(m, (1.0, 0.62, 0.3), 0.45). Give the street's own lamp glass (gas_lamp_3) the same material so all lamps match. Targets: glass average 0.55-0.65, a core of at least 0.8, saturation 0.35-0.5, and the nearer left lamp at least as bright as the farther one.

findings.title: The new left lamp's head nearly touches two downpipes
findings.where: 0.348-0.369 across, 0.385-0.40 down (lamp head); downpipes at 0.336 and 0.379 across on the left house fronts
findings.what: At 0.392 down the head spans pixels 376-398. The left downpipe is at 362-364 (a 12 px gap) and the right one at 409-411 (an 11 px gap). Rule 4 needs at least 18 px on this 1080-wide frame. The post runs between the two pipes about 20 px from each. The shot checker does not see the street's own downpipes.
findings.why: Rule 4: edges that just touch make near and far things look stuck together. Once painted, the lamp will merge with the pipes into one dark fitting on the wall.
findings.fix: Line 75: move LEFT_LAMP_POST along the kerb and check in a --preview that the head and post clear both pipes by at least 18 px, or that the head covers a pipe by 18 px or more. Pipes about 46 px apart cannot fit a 22 px head cleanly, so try a nearer place where the pipes spread wider on screen, such as y 38. By my projection that puts the head at about 0.25 across, 0.38 down, the reference's place. Let the handcart overlap the foot by at least 20 px. Re-run the checker's rule 4 with the cart, bins and sacks.

findings.title: The drum is the second-strongest shape: bigger than the reference's and more orange
findings.where: Drum body, 0.46-0.67 across, 0.63-0.84 down
findings.what: Covers 3.9% of the frame against the notice's 2.1%; the checker measures it 1.22 times as wide and tall as the reference's drum. Body brightness matches the reference (0.19 against 0.21), but it is more orange: saturation 0.58 and red-minus-blue +0.18, against 0.32 and +0.09 (colour 73,43,27 against 68,50,46). It is the second-strongest shape in a blurred phone-size view. In the film, live flames, sparks, smoke and a 1.25 m glow sprite are added on top of it.
findings.why: Rule 5: the subject must win. In the reference the drum is dull rust-brown and only its fire is bright. A big orange drum plus moving fire can pull the eye off the notice in the film.
findings.fix: Painter words: 'the fire drum is a dull, dark rust-brown, not orange; only the fire inside is bright'. If it still competes in the film's end frame, desaturate the drum a little in 3D (a tint that keeps its brightness), not its size.

findings.title: The corner lamp's top-left corner meets the house's eave bracket and the winding rope's end
findings.where: About 0.75-0.78 across, 0.23-0.25 down
findings.what: Since the lamp moved left, its glass's top-left edge (pixel 831-837 across) sits directly against a dark bracket on the right-hand house (0.02-0.06 brightness right up to its edge at 0.245 down). The rope from the right winding wheel ends at that bracket about 24 px left of the lamp's corner, so the rope seems to tie on to the lamp.
findings.why: Rule 4: a near-tangent where the pit column hands over to the notice column. The painter may fuse lamp, bracket and rope into one fitting. It might also read as a useful line from pit to notice, so it is a judgement call.
findings.fix: Painter words: 'the gas lamp stands free on its own post; the rope from the winding wheel runs to the house wall, not to the lamp'. Only if the plate shows them fused, nudge LAMP_POST about 0.1 m right (x 3.82) and recheck rule 7 (lamp centre within 0.07 of the notice's).

findings.title: The gutter and kerb at the frame's entry still look stepped
findings.what: Stripe contrast halved: fine-detail spread 0.054 to 0.027 at the bottom and 0.031 to 0.025 higher up. Part of that comes from the darker light. The stacked slab look is still plain by eye. The reference has one clean kerb line and a smooth gutter here.
findings.why: This is where the eye enters the frame. The kerb is the leading line from the bottom-left toward the drum and the notice, and the steps break it.
findings.fix: Painter words: 'the gutter beside the kerb is a shallow, smooth stone channel: no steps, no grating'. The other critic covers the 3D side.

findings.title: At phone size only the notice's heading reads comfortably
findings.where: Notice lettering, 0.715-0.875 across: 'NOTICE' at 0.523-0.534 down; 'PITS WILL BE CLOSED' at 0.571-0.576; 'NEW TERMS' at 0.590-0.595
findings.what: Ink heights on the 1920-tall frame: 'NOTICE' 23 px; 'PITS WILL BE CLOSED' and 'NEW TERMS' 11 px each. On a 6.1-inch phone held at 35 cm that is about 16 and 8 minutes of arc. 8 is about 1.6 times the eye's limit: readable with effort, not at a glance. The notice is 2.1% of the frame against the reference's 3.4%. That is its shape (1.4 to 1 against 2.06 to 1), a content change the earlier critics already put off.
findings.why: The end frame is the notice's biggest moment in the film. The film's own titles (LOCKED OUT / FROM 1 MAY 1926) carry the message, so the notice need only be recognised.
findings.fix: Keep the hold on the composed frame at least the planned 3.5 s (8.5-12 s). No change to 3D.

findings.title: The pail sits in the band where video apps put captions
findings.where: Pail 0.68-0.87 across, 0.82-0.94 down
findings.what: Reels, TikTok and Shorts lay caption and account text over roughly the bottom fifth of the frame, left and centre. The pail falls inside it, as do the chair's feet (to 0.876 down). Rule 12 in the checker covers only the right-hand button strip. The notice, the lantern and the drum's mouth are all above 0.76.
findings.why: Only the least important story prop is at risk.
findings.fix: Nothing to change; keep any burned-in captions out of the lower right.

- I ran no Blender and no film render. Every target value is an estimate from the measured brightness and the light settings, not a test render. In particular, I did not check:
  - how the film page's fireLight, noticeGlow, glow sprite, flames and 0.3 vignette change the notice's warmth, the balance or which thing the eye goes to first;
  - what fills the colliery doorway in street.blend;
  - whether Blender 5.x EEVEE needs a render-method change for the glass transparency;
  - why the extra lit window did not appear (my [::2] explanation is a likely cause, not a confirmed one).
- How I measured:
  - Prop masks come from next/next26/ids.png (15:52). They line up with this still: for example, the lamp post's lowest visible pixel sits behind the board, and the per-prop numbers are consistent. They were not re-rendered for this exact run.
  - The reference's boxes were placed by hand (about ±0.01).
  - Brightness is Rec.709 luma on 0-1 values; 'warmth' is red minus blue.
  - The eye-order judgement combines my own look at phone size (360 x 640) and blurred, the brightest-3% split, and a rough centre-surround contrast map. It is not a real eye-tracking model.

critics.summary:
Verdict: not ready for the paid repaint yet. One fault must be fixed in 3D first, and the painter needs a strict brief. The new plate (notice-corner-plate-2.png, finished 16:42, no shadow faults in its log) has the same light as the still: frame 0.207 against 0.212, notice paper 0.729 against 0.733. Everything below holds for both.

Worst fault: the drum's mouth. It is one flat burnt-orange colour (RGB 128,62,0; brightness 0.28; almost no variation from pixel to pixel) inside a pale rim that is as bright as the notice (0.74 against 0.73). A painter will read that as a pot of orange soup or paint, or an enamel lid. The film's live flames would then stand on it. The cause is the new liner: it only glows, with a black base, so nothing shades it. From both cameras the coals sit too low to be seen.

Second: anything the painter adds near a near prop breaks during the slide. Flames painted over the drum land on the kerb 6.6 m behind it and slide about 44 px off by the end. Halos, smoke, a pail handle or longer shadows close round a prop flip to the behind painting early in the move, so they blink out. The picture the user liked has exactly these extras, so the brief must forbid them.

Should-fix in 3D, each a few lines:
- The colliery doorway is still pure black (0.021, the same as before the yard light was added). The shut gates vanish inside it, so the gate reads as open, right beside where the lines meet. The yard light sits behind the gates and lights their backs.
- The drum's right edge runs 2 to 3 px from the board's left post for about 160 px of height, and stays within 12 px of it through the whole slide.
- The step-like bands in the gutter and kerb are still there; the bump-map change halved them but did not remove them.
- The gas-lamp glass and the lantern glass are flat amber cards with no flame showing. The pool of lantern light on the seat (0.84) is brighter than the lantern glass that casts it (0.54).
- The street's own far lamp is near-white (peak 0.98) beside the new amber lamp, and its post runs exactly along a house downpipe.

Confirmed fixed: the orange patch on the house wall (0.155 now against 0.244), and the lamp post's black foot (hidden behind the board). The checker's left-weight shortfall is not a painter risk.

Painter instructions (one paragraph): Repaint this exact picture in a painted documentary-illustration style: a pit-village street at dusk on 1 May 1926. Keep every shape, outline, size and position exactly where it is, and keep the picture's pattern of light and dark; change only the brushwork and colour handling. Keep the rusty oil drum with its open top; the pale grey kitchen chair with the small hurricane lantern on its seat; the wooden pail, with no handle, in front of the chair legs; the dark timber board on two posts with the cream notice; the black gas lamp on its post above the board; the brick terraces, the colliery building, its chimney and winding wheels; and the small handcart, coal sacks and dustbins far up on the left (the handcart is seen from behind). Paint the inside of the drum as a dark, sooty hollow with only a faint orange glow low down just behind its front rim, and its rim as a dull rusty lip. The colliery gates are shut: a row of thin dark iron bars standing right across a dim grey doorway. The notice is plain cream paper with grey rows of print-like marks and no readable letters. Every gas lamp has the same warm amber glass with a small bright mantle; the lantern has amber glass with a small flame inside. The gutter beside the kerb is a smooth, shallow stone channel with no steps, ridges or grating. The road, pavement and walls are cool blue-grey dusk, and warm light stays only where it already is: round the drum, on the board, on the chair seat, at the lamps and the few lit windows. Nothing is brighter than the notice. Thin parts (the lantern's wire handle, lamp arms, gate bars, chair rungs) stay thin and exactly in place, or are left out. Where two things meet or nearly meet (the drum's side and the board's left post, the lamp head and the wall pipe, the chair back across the notice's bottom), keep each edge exactly where it is and never join them. Never add: flames, sparks, smoke or steam anywhere (not from the drum, not from any chimney); glows, halos or light rays round any light, the notice or the drum; a handle on the pail; people, animals or birds; extra props (no coal tub, rails, barrel, crates or litter in the road or on the pavement); puddles or reflections; a moon, stars or bright clouds; new signs or lettering; new or longer shadows.

Measuring scripts (m1.py to m8.py, proj.py, slide.py, flames.py) and crops are in SCRATCH/plan3/corner/critique-32/work-before-the-repaint/.

critics.summary:
Verdict: for the period, the still is mostly right, and the story mostly reads. I measured the finished still (composed-end-5.png) and looked at the finished plate (notice-corner-plate-2.png, 16:42; its log has 0 "Shadow buffer full" lines). The plate shows the same faults as the still.

What is right for 1 May 1926:
- The notice. Its full text (in paint_prop_pictures.py) is dated Friday 16 April 1926. It gives the end of the Government subsidy as the reason, ends contracts on Friday 30 April and closes the pits from Saturday 1 May "until the Workmen are prepared to accept the NEW TERMS". The weekdays are correct; I checked them with Python. The type faces are the fat face and slab-serif poster types of a provincial printer.
- Lit gas lamps and a few warm upstairs windows (oil or gas light, no electric white) suit dusk on the first day.
- The hurricane lantern is the right lamp. A miner's flame safety lamp would have stayed in the colliery lamp room, so don't swap in safety-lamp.glb.
- The handcart, the dark coal sacks and the galvanised dustbins are plausible for the first day. Coal ran short only in the weeks after.
- The colliery stack with no smoke reads as idle.

The story reads from the top down. The notice comes first, then the empty chair with its lit lantern beside the fire. It says "someone sat watch here and has just stepped away". The lit lantern says they mean to come back; the empty street adds "gone".

Four things weaken it:
1. The shut colliery gates don't read. Their bars vanish against a pitch-black doorway (brightness 0.019) at 0.575-0.635 across, 0.415-0.465 down, right beside where the street's lines meet. It reads as an open black entrance, and a painter will paint one.
2. The notice's key words are small on a phone. In the end frame, the capital letters of "PITS WILL BE CLOSED" and "NEW TERMS" are 11 px tall. The picture the user liked has 18 and 22 px at the same width. Without those words, an empty chair with a lit lamp can also read as a memorial.
3. The drum's mouth is a perfectly flat orange disc: rows at 0.636-0.642 down measure 0.280 brightness with a spread of 0.002. It reads as a lid or a drum of orange liquid, not a fire burning low.
4. The corner and left gas lamps are flat amber cards with no glowing mantle (about 0.51 brightness, peak 0.60). They stand beside the street's own lamp, which is bright cream (0.81) and only 8 m away on the same kerb.

Items 1, 3 and 4 should be fixed before the paid repaint. Item 2 can wait: the notice is its own surface in the film, so it can be fixed after painting.

Smaller points:
- The gutter still has its step-like stripes.
- The chair looks like a modern painted chair.
- The brick is cleaner and redder than a soot-darkened pit village.
- To British eyes, an oil-drum brazier says 1984 more than 1926.
- An optional pick by the chair would tie the empty chair to the notice's own line about tools.

My scripts and crops are in SCRATCH/plan3/corner/critique-32/work-period-and-story/ (crop.py, measure.py, measure2.py, measure3.py, letters.py, letters_ref.py, crops/).

confirmed.title: The lamp and lantern glass are flat opaque cards because the 'see-through' setting never took effect

confirmed.evidence: Corner lamp glass: 0.51 in every row, opaque, no mantle visible (work-skeptic/lamp_head_x3.png). skeptic.painter_instructions: Repaint this exact picture as a painted documentary illustration: a pit-village street at dusk on 1 May 1926. Keep every shape, outline, size and position exactly where it is. Keep the camera and framing, and keep the picture's pattern of light and dark; change only the brushwork and the colour handling. Keep: the rusty oil drum with its open top; the empty old wooden kitchen chair, its paint pale, worn and grubby (darker than the notice), its back to the board and a small hurricane lantern on its seat; the wooden pail at the chair's feet, with no handle; the dark timber notice board on its two posts with the cream notice; the black gas lamp standing free on its own post above the board; the brick terraces, the colliery building, its chimney and winding wheels; and, far up on the left, the small two-wheeled handcart seen from behind, the coal sacks and the dustbins. The drum is dull, dark rust-brown, not orange. Its open top is a dark, sooty hollow with only a faint orange glow low down just behind the front rim, and its rim is a dull rusty lip. The colliery gates are shut: thin dark iron bars standing right across a dim grey doorway whose big doors are closed. No open tunnel, no lit door. The notice is plain cream paper with grey rows of print-like marks and no readable letters. Every gas lamp has the same warm amber glass with a small bright gas mantle inside (no candle flame). The lantern has amber glass with a small flame inside. The gutter beside the kerb is a shallow, smooth stone channel with no steps, ridges or grating. The road, pavement and walls are cool blue-grey dusk, and the brick is weathered and greyed by coal smoke without getting any darker. Warm light stays only where it already is: round the drum, on the board, on the chair seat, at the lamps and in the few lit windows. Nothing is brighter than the notice. Thin parts (the lantern's wire handle, the lamp arms, the gate bars, the chair rungs, the winding rope) stay thin and exactly in place, or are left out; never thicken them. Where two things meet or nearly meet, keep each edge exactly where it is and never join them: the drum's side and the board's left post; the gas-lamp head and the wall pipe and bracket beside it; the far lamps and the house downpipes; the chair back across the bottom of the notice. The winding rope never joins the lamp. Never add: flames, sparks, smoke or steam anywhere (not from the drum, not from any chimney); glows, halos or light rays round any light, the notice or the drum; a handle on the pail; people, animals or birds; extra props (no coal tub, rails, barrel, crates or litter in the road or on the pavement); puddles or reflections; a moon, stars or bright clouds; new signs or lettering; new or longer shadows.
